findings.finding: The Step 0 completeness-check command uses the character class `[a-z]` to match method names, which excludes every underscore-prefixed method (`_create_issue`, `_post_comment`, `_update_fields`, etc.). In practice, nearly all Cloud transport mutation methods are private and start with a single underscore, so the command would return an empty or near-empty set and the executor would incorrectly conclude all candidate methods have been accounted for — the most important part of the enumeration silently vanishes.
findings.location: Approach section, 'Completeness check for the table' — git grep command: `git grep -n "^    def [a-z]" -- ...`
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace the pattern with `"^    def [a-z_]"` — i.e.:
```
git grep -n "^    def [a-z_]" -- \
  src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py \
  src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py \
  src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py
```
This captures both public (`create_issue`) and private (`_create_issue`) methods. If dunder methods should also be excluded from the mutation table, add an explicit exclusion note — but do not accidentally exclude all underscore-prefixed names.

findings.finding: The plan explicitly prescribes `git grep` over the four transport-layer files as the method for building both the mutating-member list AND (implicitly) the dispatch-level classification table. Grep over those four files cannot discover callers in `dispatch_one.py`, `dispatch_apply_phases.py`, `apply_outbound.py`, `binding_store.py`, `apply_inbound.py`, or `apply_inbound_records.py` — which is exactly where the dispatch-level context lives. Concretely: `client.add_comment` appears across at least four call sites with different dispatch contexts (single-attempt in `dispatch_apply_phases.py:158` and `dispatch_one.py:460,657`; `_call_with_retry`-wrapped in `apply_outbound.py:215`); `client.add_label` appears without `_call_with_retry` at `binding_store.py:702` in addition to the three wrapped call sites in `dispatch_one.py`. None of these caller-side dispatch-level facts are reachable by grepping only the transport files. The plan says to 'Determine this by reading the call site' but the prescribed enumeration command reads only the transport files, not the call sites.
findings.location: Step 0 / 'Completeness check for the table' section: 'git grep -nE "^(    )?def [a-z]" -- src/...acli.py src/...acli_graph.py src/...acli_rest.py src/...acli_cli_ops.py'

`add_label`'s dispatch-level classification would omit `binding_store.py:702`, which calls `client.add_label` directly without `_call_with_retry`, representing a fourth dispatch context (no wrapper) that the grep-over-transport-files method cannot find.

Any mutating member added to the transport files in the future (or any existing member called from a newly discovered caller) will silently be assigned an incorrect dispatch classification if the table derivation method is grep-only over the transport layer.
findings.suggested_fix: For each mutating transport member, run `find_referencing_symbols('<member_name>')` to get every structural reference, then separately `grep -rn 'member_name'` across the full reconciler tree (not just the four transport files) to catch string-based dispatch and monkeypatching. The dispatch-level column in the table must be derived from these call-site results, not from reading the transport file bodies.
